summary: Munish Chandra Joshi was an archaeology, history, and Indology scholar. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1987–1989) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1998–2004).
Munkhjavkhlan Baatar is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at the National University of Mongolia, where he later held an academic post.

Murray Barnson Emeneau was a linguistics and Indology scholar. Educated at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Edgerton, Sturtevant, and Sapir, he taught at Yale (1926–1939) and was Assistant Professor of Sanskrit and General Linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Murray Fowler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Minnesota, Oregon, Vienna, and Harvard under Joshua Whatmough, he held posts at Pomona, Purdue, Harvard, and as Associate Professor of comparative philology at UW–Madison (1946–1953).

Musashi Tachikawa works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Nagoya and Harvard under Ingalls, Nagatomi, and others. His career includes posts at Nagoya, the National Museum of Ethnology (~1992–2005), and Aichi Gakuin University (~2005–2012).

Muzaffar Alam is a historian and Indologist who studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, AMU, and JNU. He taught at JNU (~1973–2001) before becoming the George V. Bobrinskoy Professor in South Asian Languages and Civilizations at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon was a linguist and Indologist who studied at UCD, Berlin, Bonn, and Paris under scholars including Meillet, Thurneysen, and Zimmer. He taught at TCD, UCL, Wisconsin, Chicago, and Edinburgh, and directed the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myosei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Ryukoku University, attested as Professor in 1987 and later as Professor Emeritus in 2015.

Mysore Hiriyanna was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College. He spent much of his career at Maharaja's College, Mysore, as Professor of Sanskrit (~1912–1927), and served as Professor at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford under Ghurye, Radcliffe-Brown, and Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Baroda, Delhi, and the Institute for Social and Economic Change (Chairman 1972–1979).

Mário Bruno Cruz is an architect and translator active in Buddhist studies. He studied at NOVA University of Lisbon and the University of Lisbon, working as an architect and as a translator for multiple publishing houses and cultural foundations.

Mélanie Vandenhelsken specializes in Tibetology and religious studies, holding a doctorate from the University of Montpellier. She has held posts at Montpellier, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, the University of Vienna, Webster Vienna Private University, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Mónika Kiss is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued her PhD in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University under the guidance of Masanori Yamaji, Robert F. Rhodes, and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Gore was an Indology scholar who served as Librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and later as Librarian at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as Professor at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He held positions at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College, Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, and Visva-Bharati University.

N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg, Strasbourg, Berlin, and Bonn under Jacobi and Leumann. He held posts at Moscow State University, Saint Petersburg State University, Irkutsk, and the Asiatic Museum.
N. J. Karthika is an Indologist working in computational fields. She completed her PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and subsequently held an academic post there.

N. Lakshminarayana Rao was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He served the Government of India as Special Officer for Epigraphy in 1956 and held the post of Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India.
